intro.text: A spearman squadleader in Brightlord Amaram's army, called Stormblessed, who fights to keep every man in his squad alive.
A branded slave and former spearman, assigned as a bridgeman to Bridge Four in Highprince Sadeas's army on the Shattered Plains.
A former slave and bridgeman who swore the Second Ideal of the Windrunners and became captain of Highprince Dalinar Kholin's guard, leading the men of Bridge Four.
A Windrunner of the returning Knights Radiant and captain of Dalinar Kholin's guard, commanding the former bridgemen of Bridge Four.
A Windrunner of the Knights Radiant from Alethkar who took Jezrien's place as a Herald when the Oathpact was restored.

items.text: Kaladin, called Kal as a boy, grew up in Hearthstone as the son of the town surgeon Lirin, close to his younger brother Tien and to Laral, the citylord's daughter. He began training in surgery at eight while dreaming of being a soldier, and argued with his father, who wanted to send him to Kharbranth to study.

In his first quarterstaff fight against an older boy, Kal showed natural skill but stopped once he had hurt his opponent. The dying citylord Wistiow left him spheres to pay for his studies. When a young girl he tried to treat alone died, he told his father he did not want to be a surgeon.

The new citylord Roshone arrived in Hearthstone, blamed Lirin for his posting, and squeezed the family's income, believing Lirin had stolen Wistiow's spheres. After a humiliating dinner at the manor, Kal realized his father had indeed taken them, and decided to become a surgeon so he could stand up to the lighteyes.

Kal and Lirin saved Roshone after a hunting accident while his son died. Soon after, Brightlord Amaram arrived to recruit soldiers, and Roshone put Tien on the conscription list. Unable to take his brother's place, Kaladin enlisted alongside him, promising his parents he would bring Tien home.
Tien was placed in a reserve squad and sent to the front lines as bait. Kaladin ran across the battlefield, killing for the first time, but reached his brother only after he died.

In his final battle in Amaram's army, Kaladin's carefully drilled squad avoided losses even as the wider battle collapsed. He single-handedly killed six men to rescue the young recruit Cenn, then led his men in killing an enemy battalionlord, hoping the feat would earn him a transfer to the Shattered Plains.

An enemy Shardbearer then cut through Amaram's army, killing Cenn, Dallet, and most of Kaladin's squad before going after Amaram. Kaladin finally killed him, but, sickened by the weapon that had slain his friends, refused the Shards and gave them to one of his men.
Amaram summoned Kaladin hours after the battle, had his surviving squadmates killed, and took the Shards for himself. As a mercy, he spared Kaladin but branded him a slave.
As a slave, Kaladin made repeated escape attempts. Rather than having him killed for the last one, his master branded his forehead with the shash glyph, meaning dangerous, and sold him.

Bought by the slaver Tvlakv, Kaladin reached his lowest point, secretly keeping poisonous blackbane leaves while his attempt to save a sick fellow slave failed. A strangely persistent windspren began speaking to him, even using his name. The caravan finally brought him to the vast army camps of the Shattered Plains.

Tvlakv sold Kaladin to Sadeas's army, where his reputation as a troublemaker got him assigned to Bridge Four, the crew with the worst casualty rate. Thrown unprepared into a bridge run, he survived the Parshendi volleys at the front. When he nearly gave up afterward, the windspren urged him to move and introduced herself as Sylphrena.

As bridgemen kept dying around him, Kaladin sank into despair and went to the Honor Chasm intending to jump. Syl returned and begged him to try once more. He took the post of bridgeleader from the sergeant Gaz by force and bribery, then learned the name of every man in Bridge Four.

Kaladin forced Bridge Four into training, took the most dangerous spot on the bridge himself, and insisted on bringing the wounded back to camp. When the army refused to feed injured bridgemen, he gathered knobweed for antiseptic with help from Rock and Teft, the first of his men to trust him.

Kaladin trained Bridge Four to carry the bridge on its side as a shield. It protected his men, but other crews copied it badly and Sadeas's assault failed. As punishment he was hung outside during a highstorm. In the storm he glimpsed a vast face and drew Light from a sphere. He survived, and his men began calling him Kaladin Stormblessed.

Realizing that bridgemen were deliberately used as bait, Kaladin despaired, and when Bridge Four was sent to permanent chasm duty he proposed training them as spearmen in order to escape. He secretly drilled them in the chasms, making Teft, a former soldier, oversee their progress.

After Dunny's death, Kaladin began rescuing wounded men from other crews. When Teft tested him, he learned he had been drawing in Stormlight and feared he was cursed. A wandering storyteller told him the tale of the Wandersail and asked him to look after Sigzil. Syl admitted she was the cause of his powers, and Kaladin chose to accept the responsibility and use them to help others.

With Teft teaching him the First Ideal, Kaladin practiced his abilities. When Bridge Four was put on every run, he wore armor made from Parshendi carapace and ran ahead as a decoy, drawing the enemy's fury while Stormlight protected him. Dalinar Kholin's forces saved the bridgemen from an ambush afterward.

At the Battle of the Tower, Sadeas withdrew and left Dalinar's army trapped. Kaladin planned to use the retreat to fake Bridge Four's deaths, but after Syl revealed she was an honorspren, he turned the men back. He pulled a whole volley of arrows into his shield, then spoke the Second Ideal of the Windrunners.

Fighting with enhanced skill, Kaladin held the bridge, sent Adolin to safety, and rescued Dalinar from a Parshendi Shardbearer. Back in camp, Dalinar traded his Shardblade to Sadeas for the bridgemen's freedom, and Kaladin became captain of Dalinar's guard.

Kaladin organized the former bridgemen into a force, promoting his closest men to lieutenants while Bridge Four guarded Dalinar. The men tattooed over their slave brands, but Kaladin's Stormlight healed his tattoo away. Refusing to reveal his powers, he and his men stripped off their Cobalt Guard insignia and declared themselves Bridge Four.

Kaladin's duties expanded to guarding Dalinar's family and the king. With Sigzil, Rock, and Lopen he began testing his Surgebinding in the chasms. Returning to camp, he learned that Amaram, the man who had branded him, had arrived on the Shattered Plains.

Kaladin sparred with the ardent swordmaster Zahel and lost a reckless brawl with Adolin. After a sabotaged balcony nearly killed Elhokar, Kaladin told Dalinar about Amaram's betrayal, but Dalinar only agreed to look into it, leaving Kaladin angry.

Warned by Syl, Kaladin helped Dalinar and the king flee when Szeth attacked. Kaladin's arm was severed, but he pushed Szeth and Dalinar through a hole in the wall, survived the fall, and healed himself with Stormlight, shocking Szeth into retreat. With Beld dead and Hobber maimed, Kaladin asked Zahel to train him.

Kaladin learned to Lash himself to walls and let Renarin join Bridge Four. Training under Zahel, he also listened to Moash's hatred of the king, and was introduced to Graves and his conspirators, who asked him to help assassinate Elhokar. He hesitantly agreed, to Syl's dismay.

Alone in the chasms, Kaladin learned to fly. He nearly went to kill Amaram but turned back at Syl's plea, and Shen revealed his true name, Rlain, before leaving. Guarding Adolin on an outing with Shallan, Kaladin met Wit again, then heard Dalinar announce Amaram as leader of the refounded Knights Radiant.

When Adolin faced four Shardbearers in a duel, Kaladin leapt into the arena to help him. He cracked Shardplate with a Lashing-enhanced kick, caught a Shardblade between his hands, and forced opponents to yield, helping Adolin win.
When Adolin was granted a boon, Kaladin publicly challenged Amaram for his crimes. The humiliated king had him arrested, and he was imprisoned, vowing never to trust a lighteyes again.

In prison, Kaladin heard Wit tell the story of Fleet and came to believe Elhokar had to die. When finally released, he found Adolin had jailed himself in protest. He refused the Shards Adolin had won and gave them to Moash instead.

On a scouting expedition a sabotaged bridge dropped Kaladin and Shallan into the chasms. With Syl gone and his powers failing, he traveled with her, they shared painful pasts, and he used her Shardblade to kill a chasmfiend before they sheltered from a highstorm in a cut alcove and returned to camp.

Recovering in camp, Kaladin watched Dalinar make Amaram confess but let him go. During the Weeping, Elhokar visited Kaladin and apologized for imprisoning him, and Kaladin realized the king was to Dalinar what Tien had been to him.

Rushing to the palace, Kaladin found the conspirators striking at Elhokar. Moash and Graves, in Shardplate, beat him down, but he stood again in front of the wounded king and spoke the Third Ideal of the Windrunners.

Kaladin flew to Hearthstone to warn his family of the Everstorm but arrived after it struck. He reunited with his parents, punched Roshone for Moash's sake, and met his new baby brother, Oroden. Learning the town's parshmen had fled, he promised to return and set out after them.

Tracking the escaped parshmen through Hornhollow, Kaladin found them frightened and playing cards rather than monstrous, and surrendered instead of fighting. Traveling as their captive, he taught them to cook, bind wounds, and make tools, and came to see them as former slaves like himself.

In Revolar, a yellow spren asked whether Kaladin would fight for the parshmen. When a red-eyed Fused appeared, he fled and shielded a group of townspeople from it before the winds carried him to Urithiru.

Back at Urithiru, Kaladin trained Bridge Four and new recruits in drawing Stormlight, and helped Hobber heal his legs. At a meeting of Radiants he argued with Jasnah that the parshmen only wanted a place to live, and he also drew out Rlain, who felt isolated.
Dalinar declared Kaladin a lighteyes as a Shardbearer and granted him lands. Kaladin flew Elhokar, Adolin, Shallan, and others above a highstorm to Kholinar, where they entered the city in disguise.

On Elhokar's orders, Kaladin joined Kholinar's Wall Guard, finding a sense of belonging among its soldiers and trading guarded words with its leader, Highmarshal Azure. During an assault he killed a Fused, the first the guard had seen fall, and won Azure's support for an attack on the palace.

Kaladin rescued Elhokar's young son from the palace but froze when his friend Sah's parshmen and the human guards fought each other. Moash then killed Elhokar in front of him. Shallan activated the Oathgate, and the group found themselves in Shadesmar.
Brooding and depressed, Kaladin crossed Shadesmar with Adolin, Shallan, Azure, and their spren. At a lighthouse he touched a glowing globe and saw a vision of Dalinar in danger and of Thaylen City.

When Syl surrendered to honorspren to save the group, Kaladin raged at her captivity. Contemplating the Fourth Ideal, windspren began gathering around him, and he felt afraid of what it would demand. Racing for the Thaylen City Oathgate, he fought pursuing Fused until his Stormlight ran out, still not ready to speak the Ideal.
Returning to the Physical Realm, Kaladin blocked Amaram's killing blow at Dalinar. He fought the transformed, empowered Amaram while fending off Fused, until Rock shot Amaram with an arrow.
After the battle, Kaladin talked with Syl and Teft, then flew to southern Alethkar, where Skar and Drehy had hidden young Gavinor among refugees.
As the war spread, Kaladin was stretched across battlefronts while overseeing Windrunner training, and was promoted to highmarshal.
When Navani sought Windrunners to find the Oathgate in Akinah, Kaladin sent Lopen, Huio, and Cord to learn whether it still worked and whether the enemy held it.

Returning to Hearthstone to extract a rebel general, Kaladin barely survived a Fused who could travel as a streak of light. He then brought an airship to evacuate the whole town, knowing his parents would never abandon its people.
Defending the airship, Kaladin fought the Heavenly One Leshwi in formal duels, spared a Fused he had beaten, and fought Leshwi to a draw.

In the manor's cellar Kaladin found Moash killing Roshone. Moash surrendered, then urged Kaladin to kill himself, and Kaladin froze until Renarin appeared and brought him back to the airship, deeply shaken.
Worried by his growing struggles, Dalinar relieved Kaladin of active duty while letting him keep his rank. Kaladin argued at first but accepted that he needed a break.
That night Adolin refused to leave Kaladin alone and took him out. Rock then said farewell, leaving with his family to face his people's judgment.
Kaladin passed his roles to Sigzil and Skar. Zahel defeated him in a sparring match and told him he could not become an ardent because he still loved fighting.

When his parents arrived at Urithiru, Kaladin revealed his retirement and began working as a surgeon alongside Lirin, which kept him busy and eased his sadness. Teft, struggling with his addiction, stayed with him.

Finding a depressed soldier, Noril, locked away by ardents, Kaladin saw that he too could have ended up there. He began group sessions for men with battle fatigue and admitted they were helping him as well.

When the Fused seized Urithiru, nearly every Radiant fell unconscious except Kaladin. To protect Teft and his family he fought, killed a Regal, and fled into hiding high in the tower, pursued by the Pursuer. In a hidden room he made contact with Navani and planned a resistance.

Helped by Dabbid and the tower's spren, the Sibling, Kaladin spied on the Oathgates and destroyed a node the Fused had found. His healing faltered as the corruption spread, and Navani gave him a fabrial glove to replace his weakened Lashings.

After destroying a node in the well and escaping onto the tower's exterior during a highstorm, Kaladin collapsed into a coma, his mind drawn toward Odium. There Wit hid him briefly and told him a story.

Healed by Lift, Kaladin defeated and humiliated the Pursuer, but then found Teft dead at Moash's hands. Broken, he killed the Pursuer in a rage and chased the Heavenly One who had taken his father up the tower.
Atop Urithiru, Kaladin jumped, meaning to die. Dalinar drew him into a vision of Tien, who helped him accept loss. Still falling, Kaladin spoke the Fourth Ideal, and windspren formed his Shardplate.

After Teft's funeral, Kaladin asked Dalinar to let him keep pursuing mental health work. In a market he found the carved horse Tien had given him, then went to a group session as he had promised Teft.
Kaladin heard a mysterious voice, the Wind, warning him of a coming storm. Meeting Wit, he admitted the wind had been asking for his help, and Wit urged him to follow it before saying goodbye.
Preparing to fly to Shinovar with Szeth, Kaladin handed leadership of the Windrunners to Sigzil and said heartfelt goodbyes to Bridge Four, assuring Rlain he would always belong.
In Azir, Kaladin declined Shallan and Adolin's request for help against an army gathering in Shadesmar. Shallan made him promise to return, and he flew to Shinovar with Szeth and Nightblood.
Chosen by the Wind, Kaladin took Jezrien's place as a Herald after his death, becoming a Cognitive Shadow known as the Herald of Kings, of the Wind, and of Second Chances.

appearance.text: Kaladin is strongly built, and his forehead bears slave brands, including the shash glyph meaning dangerous. He dislikes beards because they itch, and shaves whenever he can.

personality.text: Since childhood Kaladin has had a fierce protective instinct. He became a surgeon's apprentice and battlefield medic, joined the army to watch over Tien, and took the youngest, least trained recruits into his squad to protect them.

A natural leader and capable commander, Kaladin inspires loyalty and belief in his men. He became Amaram's youngest squadleader at eighteen, kept his squad's casualties the lowest in the army, and turned the despised Bridge Four into a motivated fighting force with almost no resources.
Betrayed by lighteyes such as Roshone and Amaram, Kaladin distrusts nearly all lighteyes, though others note he carries himself like one. He resents those qualities in himself.

Kaladin feels deep loss when those he protects die, believes himself cursed to survive, and is prone to depression, including heavy melancholy during the Weeping. At his lowest he has fallen into apathetic, suicidal despair.
